UnitStatement: The OpenPipeStress PLAN.md is a non-governing strategy document; it is the strategic map defining "done", current milestone position, roadmap posture, and how the project's authority layers relate.
PLAN.md asserts no authority of its own and creates no lifecycle, release, professional, certification, or code-compliance claim.
When PLAN.md and an authoritative surface disagree, the authority wins and PLAN.md is corrected.

Before 2026-06-13 the strategic-roadmap content was distributed across PRD.md §22, execution/_Coordination/_COORDINATION.md, and the active completion plan; PLAN.md now consolidates that durable strategic framing.
PLAN.md absorbs durable strategic framing (definition of done, milestone position, roadmap risks) so the active plans/PLAN_*.md can remain a pure tactical selection instrument.
PLAN.md does not restate the underlying authorities; it routes to them.
Why the product exists and what must remain true is authoritatively defined by INTENT.md and DIRECTIVE.md.
What must be built and the release yardstick is authoritatively defined by PRD.md §10 (functional requirements) and §22 (release milestones).
Binding invariants are authoritatively defined by CONTRACT.md.
The public/private data and protected-content boundary is authoritatively defined by IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md and PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md.
What depends on what is authoritatively defined by execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md and the approved DAG-006.
How work executes and the current target-stage standard (the "Working Desktop Application Standard") is authoritative for the stage gate in execution/_Coordination/_COORDINATION.md.
Tactical tranche selection is authoritatively held by the active plans/PLAN_2026-06-10_prd_completion.md.
Human decision preparation and rulings are authoritatively recorded in execution/_Coordination/_DECISIONS/_REGISTER.md.
The PRD defines completion through two surfaces, both treated as binding.
Completion requires R0–R5 release-milestone exit criteria (PRD §22) taken verbatim.
R5 (Engineering Beta) is the terminal milestone: external engineers can reproduce validation examples and the public repository contains no known protected standards data.
Completion requires all 16 Must functional requirements (FR-001..016) verified against their acceptance criteria.
Completion requires all 6 Should functional requirements (FR-017..022) implemented.
Completion requires the 3 Could requirements (FR-023..025) either implemented or explicitly dispositioned by a human deferral record at the R5 gate; silence is not a disposition.

Completion additionally requires human-gated governance closures the PRD and CONTRACT make prerequisites for any release claim: unit catalog acceptance, thresholds, CI/release authority, and issuance of deliverables.
The human-gated governance closures are scheduled as decisions, not assumed, per the decision register and completion plan §2.
The milestone position table moves only at milestone boundaries (human-ruled stage gates), not per tranche; per-tranche progress lives in the completion plan and plans/PLAN_COMPLETION_LOG.md.
The authoritative current target stage is R3 (DEC-035, recorded in _COORDINATION.md); the milestone-position table is a position summary, not the stage authority.
R0 (Architecture Prototype) is met in substance; its deferred Unit system is pulled onto the critical path as Phase B (B1 units crate landed 2026-06-12; B2/B3 unit-aware I/O in progress).
R1 (Core Solver MVP) is substantially met (linear static, dense solve); tolerance thresholds were RULED via DEC-024/DEC-026 (D-04).

R2 (GUI MVP) is met in substance; the exit chain was verified and the stage advanced R2→R3 (DEC-035), carrying two residuals to the R3 exit review: F-4 (completed human packaged-GUI journey, SMOKE TP-MAC-141) and the A3 authoring-journey usability finding.

R3 (Rule packs + private libraries, current target) is in progress: C1-C4 landed (expression grammar, rule-pack editor, private-library GUI, end-to-end rule checks GUI-true); remaining before R3 exit is C5 guided-workbench/packaged-journey closure for the two R2-carried residuals.

R4 (Components + nonlinear supports) is schema/data-model only; the sparse-solver strategy is decided (DEC-023, first slice landed); no bend/branch/expansion-joint/hanger elements and no assembled nonlinear iterative solve (Phase D) exist yet.
R5 (Engineering Beta) is distant; all release machinery is TBD, validation is manual, with redaction workflow and signed releases pending (Phase E).
The product is built by turning the PRD yardstick into evidenced, bounded tranches through a fixed chain of surfaces.
Intent→Requirements: INTENT.md (why / what must remain true) and PRD.md (§10 FRs and §22 milestones) define the target.
Requirements→Structure: SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md decomposes the PRD into a flat package/deliverable set, and approved DAG-006 records what depends on what.

Structure→Execution: _COORDINATION.md is the operational control plane covering the Application Integration And Issuance Loop, the staged Working Desktop Application Standard (current target stage), bounded workers, validation, evidence, and git closeout.

Execution→Selection: the active plans/PLAN_*.md orders work toward the PRD yardstick (phase plan, dependency spine, FR completion map) as selection guidance, not authority; landed detail compresses into plans/PLAN_COMPLETION_LOG.md.
Human gates throughout: _DECISIONS/_REGISTER.md tracks human-gated decisions (D-01..D-12 and successors); only humans rule them, captured as DEC/SCA records in SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md.
When a lower layer and a higher authority disagree, the discrepancy is surfaced and the lower layer (this map, the completion plan, a register) is corrected, never the authority.
A dependency graph is not a fact to be discovered but a model relative to a stated objective and edge semantics; individual edges are frequently a judgment call.
The one objective invariant, once semantics are fixed, is the strongly-connected-component (SCC) decomposition: contracting each SCC yields a unique condensation that is always a DAG.

The project builds and maintains its dependency graph by cycle-driven resolution: treating SCCs as the diagnostic of where ordering is undecided, resolving each by an explicit recorded move (decompose / invert / merge / cut), and holding cycle-participating edges non-gating until resolved.
Cycle-driven resolution localizes the subjective calls to cycle-closing edges and keeps them auditable.
A new approved DAG version is event-driven by a decomposition revision / SCA, not periodic.

The canonical cycle-driven-resolution doctrine is the shared repo-root CYCLE_DRIVEN_RESOLUTION.md; operative practice lives in _COORDINATION.md; and this project's adoption, rollout, and DAG-007 re-derivation trigger are in PLAN_2026-06-13_cycle_driven_resolution_doctrine.md.
The target stage is R3 / Phase C (DEC-035, superseding the DEC-029 hold).

Ordinary development has completed the Phase C implementation spine: C1 expression grammar freeze, C2 rule-pack editor GUI, C3 private-library management GUI, and C4 end-to-end rule checks on authored models are landed.
The next in-stage program is C5 R3 exit readiness and authoring-usability closure: guided-workbench redesign, packaged A12/R3 journey successor evidence, and an R3 exit evidence package.
The Phase B unit-aware-I/O remainder can run alongside C5 when it does not block C5.
Two blocking residuals gate any R3 exit review: F-4 (a completed human packaged-GUI journey) and the A3 authoring-journey usability finding.
C5 is the ordinary-tranche program that must prepare and record closure evidence for the two blocking residuals before any human R3 exit review can begin.
Later stages follow the completion plan: R4 (piping components and nonlinear supports) and R5 (engineering beta and release machinery).
Stage advancement is human-ruled: agents propose with evidence, and only a human-approved coordination update advances the target stage recorded in _COORDINATION.md.
The headline prohibitions live in full in the authorities; PLAN.md only names them and routes.

Code-neutral boundary: no populated code tables, no protected standards constants or copied formulas; all component factors are user-entered (INTENT.md §Non-goals, IP_AND_DATA_BOUNDARY.md, CONTRACT.md).

No professional/reliance claims: the software computes user-defined checks and never makes a compliance, certification, sealing, approval, authentication, or code-compliance claim; human acceptance stays external and hash-bound (PROFESSIONAL_BOUNDARY.md, CONTRACT).

Local-first, private-by-default: no cloud, daemon, network, telemetry, or repository-default private-data writes; user-created models stay in local project storage and are never committed; bundled examples are invented.
No silent defaults: unknown values are explicit TBD, surfaced not guessed (CONTRACT).

Roadmap risk: D-01 (units) stalls and silently re-blocks R2 value; mitigated by leading with the decision-prep tranche (RULED DEC-018) so Phase A proceeds SI-labeled and any stall is visible, not hidden.

Roadmap risk: the edit-loop (A1–A3) is the product hinge and may be underestimated; mitigated by smallest-possible tranche slicing and landing Playwright (A8) early against each increment, not at phase end.
Roadmap risk: nonlinear iteration (D6) convergence quality; mitigated validation-first by drafting D8 cases alongside D6 and reusing the existing diagnostics taxonomy per PRD §24 mitigation row.
Roadmap risk: GUI test debt compounds; mitigated by A8 making the R2 journey itself the regression spine before C/D add surface area.

Roadmap risk: release-machinery decisions (D-05..07) deferred until they block R5; mitigated by the decision register making them explicit mid-plan items with RGAP traceability, not end-loaded surprises.

Roadmap risk: scope drift via app tranches crossing deliverable boundaries; mitigated by the coordination loop rule that tranches name the app-owned slice and allowed write targets, plus register hygiene in completion-plan F3.

PLAN.md does not select tranches; the active completion plan plans/PLAN_2026-06-10_prd_completion.md holds the phase tables, dependency spine, FR completion map, and decision register that drive tranche selection under the _COORDINATION.md loop.
When a successor completion plan is accepted, the tranche-selection pointer is updated in PLAN.md and in _COORDINATION.md.
